TIAGO FERRÃO-LINDQVIST
Test & Validation Engineer | Python and SQL

tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation, transitioning into data engineering. Builds Python tools to process test-rig data, check results against specifications and produce engineering reports. Experience querying SQL Server, scheduling data processing on a lab PC and creating Power BI dashboards for engineering teams.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Data and programming: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS, SQL, SQL Server, SQLite, Power BI, Excel/VBA
Engineering and analysis: MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, LabVIEW, Minitab, design of experiments, GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving
Personal projects: Flask, Git, Docker Compose

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Test & Validation Engineer
Corvane Automotive Components | Mar 2019–Present
- Developed Python scripts to parse TDMS and CSV output from six test rigs, check channels against test specifications and generate report figures, reducing report preparation from approximately three days to half a day per test.
- Scheduled the tool to run nightly on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler. It processes approximately 2 GB of data per week and writes summary results to a SQL Server staging table created by IT. Four other test engineers use the tool.
- Built a Power BI dashboard showing pass/fail trends and cycles to failure by product generation; approximately 15 validation and design engineers use it.
- Queried the plant's test-results database for trend analysis across three product generations. Database access is primarily read-only, with write access to the staging table.
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests on seat-adjuster mechanisms and write reports for OEM customers.
- Correlate rig results with ANSYS Mechanical FEA and lead 8D root-cause analysis of field failures. Proposed an adjuster rail bracket redesign that reduced warranty returns for that part by 40%.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive to select rig load profiles matching customer duty cycles.
- Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup between 2022 and 2024.

Mechanical Design Engineer
Halvik Pumps | Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks, produced drawings with GD&T and owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Conducted structural FEA in ANSYS and changed one casing family from grey cast iron to ductile iron, reducing material cost by 12%.
- Wrote a LabVIEW acquisition program for the pump performance test bench, reducing test setup time from approximately two hours to 30 minutes.
- Supported conversion of the test bench to a Siemens S7 PLC-controlled setup, adjusting setpoints and timers in TIA Portal under an automation engineer's supervision.

PERSONAL PROJECT

Bike-sharing Trips API | 2025
- Built a small Flask API with three read-only endpoints over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite; runs locally on a laptop.
- Used Git and followed a tutorial to run the project with Docker Compose.

EDUCATION AND TRAINING
MSc Mechanical Engineering, Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

Online data engineering course | In progress
Completed 6 of 9 modules.

LANGUAGES
Portuguese: native | English: fluent | Spanish: good

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, clear and credible CV. It uses a logical structure, concise bullet points, quantified outcomes and relevant technical terminology. The strongest evidence is the Python test-data automation tool, its measurable reduction in reporting time, its use by four engineers, the SQL Server staging workflow and the Power BI dashboard used by approximately 15 engineers. The document also presents the mechanical-engineering background honestly while explaining the transition toward data engineering. The main content limitation is not poor writing: the candidate's experience is primarily engineering test-data automation rather than ownership of a senior data platform. The CV should therefore continue to make the scope of the work clear and avoid implying cloud, platform-scale or production-service experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience formatting, readable bullets, plain text contact details and searchable terms such as Python, SQL Server, Power BI, Docker Compose, Git, pandas, NumPy and SQLite. There are no tables, graphics, columns or unusual formatting that would normally interfere with parsing. Keyword coverage is good for the candidate's actual background, but the CV cannot score strongly for this specific role's AI screening because it does not show Google Cloud, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, dimensional modelling, cloud data warehouses, platform-scale operations or query optimisation. These are genuine candidate gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. The likely result is high parsing compatibility but low-to-moderate screening probability for this particular Senior Data Engineer vacancy.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's Python, SQL, BI collaboration, data-quality checking, reusable tooling, Git, Docker and learning/open-source-adjacent signals. The nightly scheduled processing tool, specification checks and dashboard demonstrate ownership, automation and practical support for engineering users. Portuguese and professional English are clearly shown. The candidate's personal project and ongoing data-engineering course support curiosity about data architecture and continued learning, although they do not establish open-source contribution experience. The principal alignment gaps are experience designing and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale, advanced Python and SQL with query optimisation on large datasets, dimensional data modelling, hands-on Google Cloud or comparable cloud experience, and graph modelling. The CV should not imply that these requirements are met.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the headline, change "Test & Validation Engineer | Python and SQL" to "Test & Validation Engineer | Python, SQL & Test Data Automation". This uses a more specific, truthful keyword phrase that reflects the strongest evidence in the CV without presenting the candidate as an experienced data-platform engineer.
2. In the Professional Summary, change "Builds Python tools to process test-rig data" to "Builds internal Python tools to process test-rig data". Adding "internal" makes the deployment scope explicit and prevents recruiters from interpreting the work as a customer-facing or cloud production platform.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Personal projects" to "Personal project technologies" or move "Flask, Git, Docker Compose" into a separate "Projects" section. This makes it unambiguous that these tools were used in a laptop-based learning project rather than in production employment.
4. In the Bike-sharing Trips API entry, retain the scope clarification "runs locally on a laptop" and change "Used Git and followed a tutorial to run the project with Docker Compose" to "Used Git and Docker Compose in a guided personal learning project." This is more concise and accurately signals the level of experience.
5. In the Corvane experience section, change "writes summary results to a SQL Server staging table created by IT" to "writes summary results to an IT-created SQL Server staging table; the main test-results database is queried primarily read-only." This consolidates the database-scope limitation next to the strongest SQL evidence and reduces the risk of overstating database ownership.
6. In the Education and Training section, change "Online data engineering course | In progress / Completed 6 of 9 modules" to "Online Data Engineering Course | In progress — 6 of 9 modules completed." This is more ATS-readable and makes the current status immediately clear.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “creating Power BI dashboards for engineering teams” — the candidate’s material supports one Power BI dashboard, not multiple dashboards.
unsupported_claims: “creating Power BI dashboards for engineering teams” — the candidate’s material supports one Power BI dashboard, not multiple dashboards.

requirements.requirement: Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Strong data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
requirements.quote: Online data engineering course | In progress; Bike-sharing Trips API personal project using Flask, Git and Docker Compose

unsupported_claims: “creating Power BI dashboards for engineering teams” — the candidate’s material supports one Power BI dashboard, not multiple dashboards.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional, well-structured CV with a credible transition narrative from mechanical engineering into data engineering. The strongest content is quantified and specific: reducing report preparation from three days to half a day, processing approximately 2 GB of data weekly, supporting four other engineers, and reducing warranty returns by 40%. The document also appropriately distinguishes workplace experience from a guided personal project and avoids overstating cloud, platform, or production-service experience. The main limitation is not writing quality but the substantial senior data-platform experience gap relative to the target role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, plain text formatting, and relevant searchable terms including Python, SQL, SQL Server, pandas, NumPy, Power BI, Docker Compose, Git, Flask, SQLite, data processing, and test data automation. It is likely to parse reliably and should achieve a moderate AI-screening probability for data engineering roles, but a lower probability for this specific Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform vacancy because it lacks supported matches for Google Cloud, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, dimensional modelling, query optimisation, and production data platforms at scale. The CV correctly does not insert unsupported keywords simply to improve ATS matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with Python-based data processing, SQL Server querying, scheduled data workflows, reporting automation, BI collaboration, problem solving, professional English, Portuguese, and evidence of ownership and delivery pace. The nightly internal tool and dashboard show useful practical data-engineering foundations, while training apprentices and supporting other engineers provide some evidence of collaboration. However, the candidate's own material shows genuine gaps against the senior role: no production data platform or cloud data warehouse experience at scale, no Google Cloud or comparable cloud experience, no dimensional modelling, no query optimisation on large datasets, and no Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka, or CI/CD experience. Graph modelling is also not present. The personal project and ongoing course provide limited but credible evidence of curiosity about data architecture and open-source technologies. The document is therefore a truthful and strong transition CV, but not yet a close match for the seniority and platform ownership expected by this vacancy.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the operational nature and scope of the strongest data-engineering experience more explicit without implying cloud or platform ownership. For example, change the second sentence to: “Builds and schedules internal Python data-processing tools that parse test-rig data, validate channels against specifications, and generate engineering reports.” Retain the existing quantified SQL Server and Power BI evidence in the following sentence.
2. In the Technical Skills section, change “SQL, SQL Server, SQLite” to “SQL, SQL Server, SQLite (read-only access to the main test-results database; writes to an IT-created staging table)” if space permits. This makes the scope of database responsibility transparent and prevents senior-level readers from inferring unsupported schema-design or database-administration experience.
3. In the Corvane Automotive Components experience, change “Scheduled the tool to run nightly on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler” to “Scheduled and supported nightly execution of the internal tool on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler.” This better communicates the operational aspect that is genuinely supported by the candidate’s portfolio, without claiming production-platform ownership.
4. In the Personal Project section, retain the wording “guided personal learning project” and consider changing the final bullet to “Used Git and Docker Compose in a guided personal learning project, running locally on a laptop.” This keeps the scope clear while making the Git and container keywords easier for ATS screening to identify.
5. In the contact line, use the complete LinkedIn URL beginning with “https://” rather than the shortened domain-only format, provided that the profile is active and accurate. This is a minor parsing and professionalism enhancement.
